title: Standard-simplex coherent mapping sets are contractible
statement:
Use standard simplices, ordinary nerves and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the subset-poset coherent realization of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. For every $r\geq0$ and vertices $0\leq i\leq j\leq r$, the enriched mapping simplicial set $\mathfrak C[\Delta^r](i,j)$ is the ordinary nerve of the inclusion-ordered poset of subsets of $\{i,\ldots,j\}$ containing $i,j$, and is weakly contractible. Every simplicial map between any two such mapping sets is a weak homotopy equivalence. In particular, for $r>0$ and $i\leq r-1$, composition with the enriched morphism corresponding to the edge $r-1\to r$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence
$$\mathfrak C[\Delta^r](i,r-1)\longrightarrow\mathfrak C[\Delta^r](i,r).$$

source.place: Definition 1.1.5.1 (printed pp. 20-21, PDF indices 37-38), and the Cartesian mapping calculation in Proposition 3.2.2.10 (printed pp. 183-184, PDF indices 200-201). Read online 2026-10-17; no Stacks tag states this coherent-realization result; archival HTT copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $0\leq i\leq j\leq r$ and let $P_{i,j}$ be the inclusion-ordered set of subsets $S\subseteq\{i,\ldots,j\}$ with $i,j\in S$. By the defining standard-simplex clause of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], $\mathfrak C[\Delta^r](i,j)=N(P_{i,j})$, with composition induced by union. The subset $m=\{i,j\}$ belongs to $P_{i,j}$ and satisfies $m\subseteq S$ for every $S\in P_{i,j}$. This includes $i=j$, when the poset has just the subset $\{i\}$.

source.place: Definition 1.1.5.1, printed pp. 20-21 (PDF pages 38-39); the mapping-poset definition and union composition.

proof.text: Write $X=N(P_{i,j})$. Define $H:X\times\Delta^1\to X$ directly in degree $n$: for a chain $S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_n$ and a weakly increasing map $\epsilon:[n]\to[1]$, its output is the chain $T_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq T_n$ with $T_k=m$ if $\epsilon(k)=0$ and $T_k=S_k$ if $\epsilon(k)=1$. This is a chain: its initial entries are $m$, the sole possible switch uses $m\subseteq S_k$, and its remaining entries are a subchain of the given chain. Restriction along every monotone $\alpha:[q]\to[n]$ gives the same formula with $S_{\alpha(k)},\epsilon(\alpha(k))$, so $H$ commutes with every face and degeneracy. Its endpoint restrictions are the constant map at $m$ and $\mathrm{id}_X$.

source.place: Definition 1.1.5.1 and Remark 1.1.5.2, printed pp. 20-21; explicit agent-written contraction of the displayed nerve.

proof.text: Let $p:X\to\Delta^0$ be the unique map and $s:\Delta^0\to X$ the vertex $m$. Then $ps=\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^0}$ and $sp$ is the constant map at $m$. Step 2 supplies the required simplicial homotopy from $sp$ to $\mathrm{id}_X$; the homotopy between $ps$ and the point identity is constant. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] with $u=p$, $v=s$, $A=X$, $B=\Delta^0$. It makes $p$ a weak homotopy equivalence, which is exactly weak contractibility. No Kan condition on $X$ is needed.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13, forward implication, with Construction 3.6.5.1 (Tag 0148) for realization; the two homotopies are the explicit ones of step 2 and the constant point homotopy.

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ be any simplicial map between two mapping sets in the statement, allowing different simplex dimensions and endpoints. Their point maps $p_X,p_Y$ are weak equivalences by step 3 and satisfy $p_Yf=p_X$. On path components, $f$ therefore induces the bijection $(p_Y)_*^{-1}(p_X)_*$. At each basepoint $x\in|X|$ and each $n\geq1$, functoriality of postcomposition gives $(p_Y)_*f_*=(p_X)_*$ on based homotopy groups, hence $f_*=(p_Y)_*^{-1}(p_X)_*$ is an isomorphism. Here the map induced by $p_Y$ uses basepoint $|f|(x)$, so all groups are correctly based. These component and group assertions are precisely the definition of weak homotopy equivalence in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Remark 1.1.5.2, printed p. 21; elementary cancellation on the component sets and based homotopy groups of the maps to a point.

proof.text: For $r>0$ and $0\leq i\leq r-1$, the edge $r-1\to r$ corresponds to the vertex $\{r-1,r\}$ of the mapping poset. By the union-composition clause of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], postcomposition is the nerve of the monotone map $P_{i,r-1}\to P_{i,r}$, $S\mapsto S\cup\{r-1,r\}$. The union contains both endpoints and lies in $\{i,\ldots,r\}$, and inclusion of subsets is preserved. Thus it is a simplicial map between exactly the two mapping sets covered by step 4, and is a weak homotopy equivalence. If $i=r-1$, its source is a point and the same formula applies; in particular $r=1,i=0$ is included.

source.place: Definition 1.1.5.1, union composition, and Remark 1.1.5.2, the edge vertex; printed pp. 20-21. The consequence is used in Proposition 3.2.2.10.

Step 1: the mapping set C[Δ^r](i,j) is the nerve of P_{i,j}, the subsets of {i..j} containing i and j; this is literally the defining paragraph in the statement of lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison, and it agrees with HTT Def 1.1.5.1 and Rem 1.1.5.2 as I know them. There is no local HTT copy, so the page numbers rest on the report's WANTED. Its least element is m={i,j}. Step 2: I checked the explicit homotopy H on N(P)×Δ^1. The output is a chain for every case of ε(k),ε(k+1) (the case 1,0 cannot occur). It is natural in every monotone α, and its endpoints are the constant map at m and the identity. Step 3: every hypothesis of lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak holds with u=p, v=s, B=Δ^0 (either endpoint order is allowed, no Kan condition), so p is a weak equivalence, which is weak contractibility by def-cbc. Step 4: cancellation from p_Y f=p_X on π_0 and on π_n at the basepoint |f|x is correct and elementary. Step 5: postcomposition with the edge r-1→r is the nerve of S↦S∪{r-1,r}, so step 4 applies; this is exactly the clause the parent lem-cbc-mapping-simplex-universal-equivalence uses for p(a)≤r-1. Small cases tested: r=0; i=j; r=1; r=2,i=0 (point→Δ^1); r=3,i=0 (edge→square). Against A–F: no cycle (the item's 499-node dependency closure does not contain it). lean.statement: theorem standard_simplex_mapping_contractible : (∀ (r : ℕ) (i j : Fin (r + 1)), i ≤ j → sHom (mk (ULift.up.{u} i)) (mk (ULift.up.{u} j)) = nerve (Path (ULift.up.{u} i) (ULift.up.{u} j)) ∧ SSet.Enhanced.IsContractible (sHom (mk (ULift.up.{u} i)) (mk (ULift.up.{u} j)))) ∧ (∀ (r s : ℕ) (i j : Fin (r + 1)) (k l : Fin (s + 1)), i ≤ j → k ≤ l → ∀ f : sHom (mk (ULift.up.{u} i)) (mk (ULift.up.{u} j)) ⟶ sHom (mk (ULift.up.{u} k)) (mk (ULift.up.{u} l)), SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence f) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Fin (r + 1)), SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (eHomWhiskerLeft SSet (mk (ULift.up.{u} i.castSucc)) (standardSimplexLastEdge.{u} r)))
